reader.decision: Approve the recommendation now: raise the TTL to 3600 and set lock_backend: redis in config/us-east.yaml. Treat an idempotent create_purchase_order in purchasing as a separate follow-up, not a replacement.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows both configs fail the same way, and the recommended change closes both timelines inside this repo. The accepted cost is an up-to-1-hour retry block after a crash. The idempotent alternative depends on purchasing, which was not checked and is outside this repo.

reconstruction.problem: restock-planner sent Halvorsen Tools two purchase orders for HT-4410. The reorder lock has a 60s TTL but the job takes about 4 minutes. In eu-west (redis) the lock expires mid-run and a second pod, started after a node restart, takes it. In us-east (lock_backend: none) acquire always returns True, so no lock exists. The ticket does not say which region ran the duplicate, and the message says that does not matter because both fail.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Two pods run the reorder loop over the same below-reorder-point list and each creates an order for HT-4410, so the supplier gets duplicate purchase orders.
reconstruction.fix: Change ttl_seconds from 60 to 3600 in planner/reorder.py and change lock_backend from none to redis in config/us-east.yaml. Pod B's SET NX then fails and it returns "skipped". The alternative is to make create_purchase_order idempotent, keyed on SKU plus date, which would need changes in purchasing.
reconstruction.cost: A pod crash mid-run blocks a retry for up to an hour, which the message judges acceptable. The lock still fails if the job ever runs longer than an hour. The cost of the idempotent alternative is not stated, because purchasing was not inspected.

reader.closing_answer: I approve raising the TTL to 3600 and switching us-east to lock_backend: redis. I do not choose the idempotent purchase order now. Check separately whether purchasing can be changed, and add it later as defence in depth.
